title: Products per category
problem: The catalogue team wants to know how many products each category contains.
objective: Return `category_name` and `product_count` (number of products in that category) for every category.
reference: SELECT c.category_name, COUNT(p.product_id) AS product_count FROM categories c LEFT JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.category_id GROUP BY c.category_name
explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps categories without products; COUNT(p.product_id) counts only matched products, so an empty category shows 0.

title: Discontinued stock still on hand
problem: Warehouse wants a list of discontinued products that still have units in stock.
objective: Return `product_name` and `units_in_stock` for discontinued products with at least one unit in stock.
reference: SELECT product_name, units_in_stock FROM products WHERE discontinued AND units_in_stock > 0
explanation: Two conditions in WHERE combined with AND: the product is discontinued and the stock is above zero.

title: Orders per shipper
problem: Logistics compares carriers by how many orders each one shipped.
objective: Return `company_name` of each shipper and `orders` (number of orders with that shipper as `ship_via`).
reference: SELECT s.company_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS orders FROM shippers s LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.ship_via = s.shipper_id GROUP BY s.company_name
explanation: Orders reference shippers through ship_via; grouping by shipper and counting order ids gives the volume per carrier.

title: Five most expensive products
problem: Pricing wants the top end of the catalogue.
objective: Return `product_name` and `unit_price` of the 5 most expensive products, most expensive first.
reference: SELECT product_name, unit_price FROM products ORDER BY unit_price DESC LIMIT 5
explanation: ORDER BY unit_price DESC sorts from the highest price; LIMIT 5 keeps the first five rows. Row order is graded.

title: Customers per country
problem: Sales leadership wants the size of each country's customer base.
objective: Return `country` and `customers` (number of customers) for countries with at least 5 customers.
reference: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customers GROUP BY country HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
explanation: GROUP BY country builds one row per country and HAVING filters the groups after counting.

title: Orders handled by each employee
problem: HR reviews order handling per employee.
objective: Return `first_name`, `last_name` and `orders` (number of orders they handled) for every employee.
reference: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS orders FROM employees e LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name
explanation: Group by the employee key (not just names, which may repeat) and count their orders.

title: Orders shipped late
problem: Customer service tracks orders that shipped after the required date.
objective: Return `order_id`, `required_date` and `shipped_date` for orders shipped after their required date.
reference: SELECT order_id, required_date, shipped_date FROM orders WHERE shipped_date > required_date
explanation: Comparing two date columns row by row; orders not yet shipped have a NULL shipped_date and drop out because NULL > date is not true.

title: Average freight by ship country
problem: Finance reviews freight cost by destination.
objective: Return `ship_country` and `avg_freight` (average freight, rounded to 2 decimals) per ship country.
reference: SELECT ship_country, ROUND(AVG(freight), 2) AS avg_freight FROM orders GROUP BY ship_country
explanation: AVG per group, then ROUND to 2 decimals as asked.

title: Revenue per category
problem: Finance wants net revenue by category (after discount).
objective: Return `category_name` and `revenue` = sum of unit_price × quantity × (1 − discount) from order lines, rounded to 2 decimals.
reference: SELECT c.category_name, ROUND(SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount))::numeric, 2) AS revenue FROM order_details od JOIN products p ON p.product_id = od.product_id JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id GROUP BY c.category_name
explanation: Order lines join to products and then categories; revenue uses the line's own unit price, not the current catalogue price.

title: Products priced above their category average
problem: Pricing flags products that cost more than the typical product in their category.
objective: Return `product_name`, `category_id` and `unit_price` for products priced above the average unit price of their own category.
reference: SELECT p.product_name, p.category_id, p.unit_price FROM products p WHERE p.unit_price > (SELECT AVG(p2.unit_price) FROM products p2 WHERE p2.category_id = p.category_id)
explanation: A correlated subquery computes each product's category average; comparing against it keeps the above-average ones.

title: Customers who never ordered
problem: Marketing wants customers with no orders at all.
objective: Return `customer_id` and `company_name` of customers who have never placed an order.
reference: SELECT c.customer_id, c.company_name FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id)
explanation: NOT EXISTS (or LEFT JOIN … IS NULL) keeps customers with no matching order; NOT IN would break if a customer_id were NULL.

title: Orders per month in 1997
problem: Operations charts monthly order volume for 1997.
objective: Return `month` (1–12) and `orders` for every month of 1997 that has orders, in month order.
reference: SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date)::int AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE order_date >= DATE '1997-01-01' AND order_date < DATE '1998-01-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
explanation: A half-open date range selects 1997; EXTRACT(MONTH …) groups by month; ORDER BY month sorts it.

title: Rank products within category by price
problem: Merchandising wants the price rank of every product inside its category.
objective: Return `category_id`, `product_name`, `unit_price` and `price_rank` (1 = most expensive in the category; ties share a rank, with no gaps).
reference: SELECT category_id, product_name, unit_price, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY unit_price DESC) AS price_rank FROM products
explanation: PARTITION BY restarts the ranking per category; DENSE_RANK gives ties the same rank without gaps.

title: Suppliers with many products
problem: Procurement reviews suppliers that provide a broad range.
objective: Return `company_name` and `products` for suppliers that supply at least 3 products.
reference: SELECT s.company_name, COUNT(*) AS products FROM suppliers s JOIN products p ON p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.company_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
explanation: Join suppliers to their products, group per supplier and keep groups with 3 or more rows.

title: Top customer per country by revenue
problem: Account managers want the biggest customer in each country.
objective: Return `country`, `company_name` and `revenue` (net, rounded to 2 decimals) of the customer with the highest revenue in each country.
reference: WITH rev AS (SELECT c.country, c.company_name, SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS r FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_details od ON od.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.country, c.company_name), ranked AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY r DESC) AS rk FROM rev) SELECT country, company_name, ROUND(r::numeric, 2) AS revenue FROM ranked WHERE rk = 1
explanation: First compute revenue per customer, then rank within country and keep rank 1 (RANK keeps ties).

title: Employees and their managers
problem: HR needs the reporting line.
objective: Return `employee` (first and last name separated by a space) and `manager` (the same for the person they report to; NULL if none) for every employee.
reference: SELECT e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee, m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name AS manager FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON m.employee_id = e.reports_to
explanation: A self join on reports_to; LEFT JOIN keeps the top manager with a NULL manager.

title: Running revenue by month
problem: Finance wants cumulative revenue through 1997.
objective: For each month of 1997 return `month` (1–12), `revenue` (net, rounded to 2 decimals) and `running_revenue` (cumulative net revenue from January, rounded to 2 decimals), in month order.
reference: WITH m AS (SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date)::int AS month, SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS r FROM orders o JOIN order_details od ON od.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= DATE '1997-01-01' AND o.order_date < DATE '1998-01-01' GROUP BY 1) SELECT month, ROUND(r::numeric, 2) AS revenue, ROUND(SUM(r) OVER (ORDER BY month)::numeric, 2) AS running_revenue FROM m ORDER BY month
explanation: Aggregate per month first, then a window SUM ordered by month accumulates it; round only at the end so totals don't drift.

title: Days between a customer's orders
problem: Retention analysts measure ordering gaps.
objective: For customer `BONAP`, return each `order_id`, `order_date` and `days_since_previous` (days since that customer's previous order; NULL for the first), in date order.
reference: SELECT order_id, order_date, order_date - LAG(order_date) OVER (ORDER BY order_date, order_id) AS days_since_previous FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 'BONAP' ORDER BY order_date, order_id
explanation: LAG looks back one row in the window ordered by date; subtracting two dates gives whole days.

title: Countries with customers but no suppliers
problem: Sourcing looks for markets without local suppliers.
objective: Return `country` for each country that has customers but no suppliers.
reference: SELECT country FROM customers EXCEPT SELECT country FROM suppliers
explanation: EXCEPT returns distinct rows from the first query that are absent from the second.

title: Products with a wide customer reach
problem: Global merchandising looks for products with wide reach.
objective: Return `product_name` and `countries` (number of distinct customer countries that ordered it) for products ordered from at least 5 different countries.
reference: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(DISTINCT c.country) AS countries FROM order_details od JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = od.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = od.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.country) >= 5
explanation: COUNT(DISTINCT country) per product, filtered in HAVING; joins go order line → order → customer for the country.

title: Orders above the customer's own average
problem: Account managers flag unusually large orders.
objective: Return `order_id`, `customer_id` and `order_total` (net, rounded to 2 decimals) for orders whose total is above that customer's average order total.
reference: WITH t AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS total FROM orders o JOIN order_details od ON od.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id) SELECT order_id, customer_id, ROUND(total::numeric, 2) AS order_total FROM t WHERE total > (SELECT AVG(t2.total) FROM t t2 WHERE t2.customer_id = t.customer_id)
explanation: Totals per order first, then compare each with the average of the same customer's totals.

title: Share of category revenue per product
problem: Category managers want each product's share of category revenue.
objective: Return `category_id`, `product_name` and `share_pct` = product net revenue ÷ its category's net revenue × 100, rounded to 2 decimals.
reference: WITH r AS (SELECT p.category_id, p.product_name, SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS rev FROM order_details od JOIN products p ON p.product_id = od.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.category_id, p.product_name) SELECT category_id, product_name, ROUND((100 * rev / SUM(rev) OVER (PARTITION BY category_id))::numeric, 2) AS share_pct FROM r
explanation: A window SUM partitioned by category gives each row its category total without collapsing rows.

title: Repeat customers across years
problem: Loyalty wants customers active in each year of the data.
objective: Return `customer_id` for customers who placed orders in at least 2 different calendar years.
reference: SELECT customer_id FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date)) >= 2
explanation: Count the distinct order years per customer in HAVING; customers active in two or more years qualify.

title: Second-best seller per category
problem: Merchandising wants the runner-up product in each category by units sold.
objective: Return `category_id`, `product_name` and `units` (total quantity sold) for the product ranked second by units within each category (ties share a rank).
reference: WITH u AS (SELECT p.category_id, p.product_name, SUM(od.quantity) AS units FROM order_details od JOIN products p ON p.product_id = od.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.category_id, p.product_name), r AS (SELECT *, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY units DESC) AS rk FROM u) SELECT category_id, product_name, units FROM r WHERE rk = 2
explanation: Rank by units per category with DENSE_RANK and keep rank 2; ties both appear.
